title: G$^2$TR: Generation-Guided Visual Token Reduction for Separate-Encoder Unified Multimodal Models
claim: Prior token-reduction methods discard tokens that matter for generation; ours keeps them and sits on the efficiency-quality Pareto frontier.
layout: 2 panels: left image-example rows, right Pareto scatter plot with highlighted star
description: The left panel is a cream rounded box with three rows, each with a colored label tag. Row 1, 'Example Task: Temporal Editing', shows a steaming pot photo, an arrow through the prompt 'Draw what it will look like after 30 minutes', and an edited pot image. Row 2, 'Motivation', shows the pot with heavy token masking from FastV, PDrop and IVC-Prune, which leaves noisy, broken images. Row 3, 'G²TR', shows the pot going through 'Using VAE latent for guidance' into a sparser mask, then 'editing' into a clean, detailed output. The right panel is a scatter plot of UMM relative average against prefill speedup. It has a blue Vanilla dot, a green IVC-Prune diamond, an orange FastV square and a red G²TR star in the upper right. A dashed Pareto front and a 'Best trade-off' arrow point to the star. The eye goes first to the pot images, then to the star.

Notably, UMM relative averages are calculated by: (understanding relative averages + editing relative averages)/2. “U” means understanding relative averages and “E” means editing relative averages (Table 2 and Table 4). Existing efforts [20, 9] mainly focus on modifying the internal architecture of UMMs, which often introduces considerable engineering complexity. In contrast, visual token reduction offers a simple and training-free alternative yet rarely explored. This naturally motivates our research question:
abstract: The development of separate-encoder Unified multimodal models (UMMs) comes with a rapidly growing inference cost due to dense visual token processing. In this paper, we focus on understanding-side visual token reduction for improving the efficiency of separate-encoder UMMs. While this topic has been widely studied for MLLMs, existing methods typically rely on attention scores, text-image similarity and so on, implicitly assuming that the final objective is discriminative reasoning. This assumption does not hold for UMMs, where understanding-side visual tokens must also preserve the model's capabilities for editing images. We propose G$^2$TR, a generation-guided visual token reduction framework for separate-encoder UMMs. Our key insight is that the generation branch provides a task-agnostic signal for identifying understanding-side visual tokens that are not only semantically relevant but also important for latent-space image reconstruction and generation. G$^2$TR estimates token importance from consistency with VAE latent, performs balanced token selection, and merges redundant tokens into retained representatives to reduce information loss. The method is training-free, plug-and-play, and applied only after the understanding encoding stage, making it compatible with existing UMM inference pipelines. Experiments on image understanding and editing benchmarks show that G$^2$TR substantially reduces visual tokens and prefill computation by 1.94x while maintaining both reasoning accuracy and editing quality, outperforming baselines on almost all benchmarks. Code is at: https://github.com/lijunxian111/G2TR.
